newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Achmea sees turnover rise by 8-10 percent.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Achmea sees turnover rise by 8-10 percent.

text.p: Dutch financial and banking group Achmea said it was expecting an eight to 10 percent increase in turnover from organic growth in 1997 and profits were expected to show an even stronger rise.
"The average organic growth of turnover is expected to be between 8 and 10 percent," said board member Marinus Jacometti.
"I can not give a forecast of our 1997 profits, but the increase is expected to outpace the rise in turnover," he said.
Jacometti added that profits were not expected to rise as strongly as in 1996 when results rose by 21.5 percent to 572 million guilders.
"That was an extraordinary year," he said.
Jacometti said that the firm was "not unhappy" with business developments during the first quarter of 1997, but declined to give more details.

For 1997 Achmea said it expected the strongest increase in turnover in the life sector as it sees an increase of 10 to 15 percent in organic growth in this business, while non-life was seen growing by three to four percent.
The banking activities, which currently account for 11.5 percent of turnover and 8.3 percent of gross profits, should increase more rapidly than other activities, Jacometti said.
"We want gross profits of our life insurance activities, health insurance activities, other non-life business and banking activities to be more in balance," Jacometti said.
Life insurance is currently good for some 50 percent of gross profits, health insurance for about 25 percent and other non-life between 11 and 12 percent.
Achmea said it was in talks about a banking acquisition in Belgium, but declined to give details on the candidate as it did not want to damage the talks.
Achmea already has banking activities in the Netherlands, Luxembourg and Belgium. The group focuses on the Benelux with its insurance and banking activites.

Achmea Holding is part of Eureko, a pan-European group of listed and unlisted insurers. Beside Achmea the group consists of Britain's Friends Provident, German Gothaer Versucherungen, Sweden's Wasa, Topdanmark of Denmark and BCP of Portugal.
